title: Counit normal form for two pasted mates with input and output arrows
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_i,\mathcal D_i$ for $i=0,1,2$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. Let $L_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$ and $R_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal C_i$ be functors with specified adjunctions $L_i\dashv R_i$, units $\eta_i$ and counits $\varepsilon_i$. For $i=1,2$ let $G_i:\mathcal C_{i-1}\to\mathcal C_i$ and $H_i:\mathcal D_{i-1}\to\mathcal D_i$ be functors and let $\alpha_i:L_iG_i\to H_iL_{i-1}$ be natural transformations. Write $\beta_i:G_iR_{i-1}\to R_iH_i$ for their mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; explicitly,
$$\beta_{i,J}=R_i(H_i(\varepsilon_{i-1,J}))\circ R_i(\alpha_{i,R_{i-1}J})\circ\eta_{i,G_iR_{i-1}J}.$$
Composition below is right to left. For any $J\in\mathcal D_0$, $Q\in\mathcal C_2$, $K\in\mathcal D_2$, and morphisms
$$b:Q\to G_2G_1R_0J,\qquad t:H_2H_1J\to K,$$
put
$$q=R_2(t)\circ\beta_{2,H_1J}\circ G_2(\beta_{1,J})\circ b:Q\to R_2K.$$
Then its counit transpose has the specified normal form
$$\varepsilon_{2,K}\circ L_2(q)=t\circ H_2H_1(\varepsilon_{0,J})\circ H_2(\alpha_{1,R_0J})\circ\alpha_{2,G_1R_0J}\circ L_2(b).$$
Both sides are morphisms $L_2Q\to K$ in $\mathcal D_2$. The functors need not be exact, and none of $\alpha_i,\beta_i,b,t$ is required to be invertible.

proof.text:
Put $X=G_2G_1R_0J$ and $Y=H_2H_1J$. The counit $\varepsilon_2:L_2R_2\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D_2}$ is natural, so its defining naturality square at $t:Y\to K$ says $\varepsilon_{2,K}\circ L_2R_2(t)=t\circ\varepsilon_{2,Y}$. Expand $q$ using preservation of composition by $L_2$ and apply this equality. Associativity of composition [def-nagata-category] gives
$$\varepsilon_{2,K}\circ L_2(q)=t\circ\varepsilon_{2,Y}\circ L_2(\beta_{2,H_1J})\circ L_2G_2(\beta_{1,J})\circ L_2(b).$$
This step is just the definition of naturality and functoriality, with $b:Q\to X$ as given.

source.place: Tags 001B (definition-functor), 001I (definition-transformation-functors), 0037 (definition-adjoint and the following unit/counit paragraph): naturality of the counit at t; agent-written boundary-arrow expansion

proof.text:
Apply [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] to $L_1\dashv R_1$, $L_2\dashv R_2$, $G_2,H_2,\alpha_2$ and $d=H_1J\in\mathcal D_1$. It gives
$$\varepsilon_{2,Y}\circ L_2(\beta_{2,H_1J})=H_2(\varepsilon_{1,H_1J})\circ\alpha_{2,R_1H_1J}.$$
Substituting into step 1 gives
$$\varepsilon_{2,K}\circ L_2(q)=t\circ H_2(\varepsilon_{1,H_1J})\circ\alpha_{2,R_1H_1J}\circ L_2G_2(\beta_{1,J})\circ L_2(b).$$

source.place: Formal properties paragraph, compatibility of mates with counits: apply the single-mate counit identity to the second square (Mathlib CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_counit, Mates.lean:123-125)

proof.text:
The component $\beta_{1,J}$ is a morphism $G_1R_0J\to R_1H_1J$ in $\mathcal C_1$. The defining naturality square for $\alpha_2:L_2G_2\Rightarrow H_2L_1$, evaluated at this morphism, is
$$\alpha_{2,R_1H_1J}\circ L_2G_2(\beta_{1,J})=H_2L_1(\beta_{1,J})\circ\alpha_{2,G_1R_0J}.$$
Replace the indicated two factors in step 2 and use preservation of composition by $H_2$. Reassociate [def-nagata-category] to obtain
$$\varepsilon_{2,K}\circ L_2(q)=t\circ H_2\bigl(\varepsilon_{1,H_1J}\circ L_1(\beta_{1,J})\bigr)\circ\alpha_{2,G_1R_0J}\circ L_2(b).$$

source.place: Tags 001I (definition-transformation-functors) at the arrow beta_1,J, and 001B (definition-functor): naturality followed by preservation of composition

proof.text:
Apply [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] to $L_0\dashv R_0$, $L_1\dashv R_1$, $G_1,H_1,\alpha_1$ and $d=J$. Its formula reads
$$\varepsilon_{1,H_1J}\circ L_1(\beta_{1,J})=H_1(\varepsilon_{0,J})\circ\alpha_{1,R_0J}.$$
Substitute it inside $H_2$ in step 3 and distribute $H_2$ over the two factors. This gives exactly
$$\varepsilon_{2,K}\circ L_2(q)=t\circ H_2H_1(\varepsilon_{0,J})\circ H_2(\alpha_{1,R_0J})\circ\alpha_{2,G_1R_0J}\circ L_2(b).$$
Each factor has the displayed source and target, so both composites are $L_2Q\to K$. Only functoriality, naturality and the two single-mate identities were used; exactness and invertibility are unnecessary.
